reading.body:
Strategic Datasphere in Alpharetta, Georgia has no confirmed operator, no working website, no published power figure, and no independent record of operation, so it cannot be counted as a data center for AI infrastructure analysis.

The address is a real two-story office building on Union Hill Road in a technology corridor where data center and network operators do exist, but research is exhausted without finding any business operating under this name. Georgia has four data centers with published power specifications totaling 66.3 megawatts, while thirty-three facilities are mapped in the state through OpenStreetMap and most publish no capacity data. Strategic Datasphere cannot be ranked among those four because it publishes no power figure and its operational status remains unconfirmed.

For AI scaling, only verified facilities with published power can inform compute capacity or grid load. This listing adds no usable capacity to that picture. The absence of evidence does not prove no facility exists, but without an operator, specifications, or third-party verification, it should not enter analysis of AI infrastructure or grid constraints.
